essence: The absent-one's initiation rite is introduced.
Enjoyment and liberation come by being led to the true guru; 'prati' signals facing-toward.
Facing-toward means becoming the seat of the guru's grace; 'worship him' names the cause of grace.
By that contact liberation is immediate — the Mālinī line's gist.
'In that instant' denies any later moment of approach; the compassionate guru must raise him at once.
Scope: one worn out by guru-service who died uninitiated, or whose longing arose at death.
Also one who took lower-tantra initiation and samaya-status but never supreme initiation.
The dead struck by ḍimba, consumed by a yogeśī's sorcery, or slain by yantra-tantra through the guru.
Even an initiate who broke samaya — redeemed through relatives' urgent entreaty.
Or of itself, by compassion stirred toward one carrying a known portion of descended power.
The guru must initiate the dead, granting Śiva; the Lord teaches this in Mṛtyuñjaya-Siddha and the rest.
For uninitiated king and commoner, the lazy, fallen, dead, child, sick, woman, aged — arrange the redemption.
The earlier rite is here abridged: no guru-worship, outward, for enjoyment, because of the case.
Consecration, caru, field, bed, maṇḍala-prep are dropped here; they serve purification and dream-vision.
The maṇḍala serves to summon and satisfy mantras; next-day god-worship does not directly aid this.
Presence arises through rite, instrument, place, maṇḍala, form, mantra, meditation, union, devotion, knowledge, identification.
For disciple, guru, and the one entered — eleven causes of presence are listed.
Each higher and freer of mixture: abundant rite, flowers, superior marks.
A single liṅga as pleasing place; the maṇḍala as trident-lotus-wheel within the mantra-circle.
Seen without invocation, the good reach samaya-status; the Mālinī calls this the accomplished samaya-maṇḍala.
'Siddha' plus 'mātra': radiant form, mantra matching it, radiant at once on sight.
Detail is not repeated; having built the maṇḍala and worshipped the god with kuśa, then —
He shapes a disciple-like form from cow-dung; one path is purified by contemplating pervasion.
Having laid it down through prakṛti, he performs the rite by great-net practice from the paths' middle.
Drawing the mind from mūlādhāra up the vast nāḍī-rod through vigor to the nose-sky, veiling with a smoke-net — the great-net practice.
This covering removes other-dependence; facing-toward at first, then led to five; the net-yoga taught in Śaṃbhunātha's āgama, for drawing the dead or the living.
Parted long, like joined armies, senses run to their own kind; nāḍī-wheels with the winds unite each to its taste, subdued by its own net.
Drawn by the great net, the knower releases the soul from heaven, ghost, animal, hell at that moment.
Gained by knowledge-mantra-yoga, this one, like an artificial yogī, drops identification from the heart of the sādhya.
States from immobile upward, wondrous nearness — all abandoned; that is no marvel.
In an eligible human body one is not yet freed; at the body's end he goes to Śiva.
Within that body Śaṅkara's supreme grace arises — from root, knowledge, or the served teacher.
Even this soul in that body, by net-force, pervades a darbha body and the rest while itself unconscious.
By abundant yoga, mantra, rite, knowledge, he then frees even the human body at once.
Though sleep-like or bodiless, the living soul drawn by the net enters the darbha body for fruit.
Jasmine-fruit and the like, or form-fashioning: by fitness within and without, this is deemed superior.
The net-brought soul stands as if asleep, lacking the mind-body apparatus.
It neither stirs nor knows nor speaks nor craves; perform all purificatory rites as before for it.
By seedless-initiation yoga, with the prior union-rite and full oblation, cast him in.
Offered into the mantra-fire in the darbha body with the full oblation, freed of bonds he reaches Śiva, never returning.
Where the darbha-born body stirs with proof, there by offering prāṇa, mind, mantra it may happen.
For the practitioner this also applies (breath-force); otherwise use the dead's redemption means.
The living absent must also be initiated, seedless: fashion a darbha-like form by net-yoga.
Draw the living soul by imagination alone, from fear of death; the rest as before, without burning kuśa.
In the sādhya, limitation, non-lordship, and niyati bind; without practice, net-drawing still frees by recognition.
If the absent were initiated unequally, the superior may be mighty; the inferior serves purification.
In the union for enjoyment, many gurus produce variety of enjoyment from varied causes.
Absent-initiation joins beyond māyā for enjoyment; craving is rare, or for its cessation.
Own consciousness outweighs other's; whatever overrides is equality and indifference.
Dharmaśiva says: for the absent, in the karma-procedure, at the full-oblation rite, if —
Fire hisses ciṭi-ciṭā, smokes, takes blue-cloud hue, flares and dies.
Terrible form, running on earth and downward; or an unheard crow-sound: then the guru marks him.
By brahmin-killing and lesser sins or their company, this unperformed-rite initiation must not be done for him.
Nine-souled, standing in the phaṭ cavity, endowed with five phaṭs: his sins I burn by eight phaṭs.
A thousand-fold fire-offering with sesame and rice; at the end the full oblation; then the guru initiates.
Purify principles up to the supreme goal, even with the sinner's paśu directly present, Bhagavān-filled.
The eldest who obtained power performs the rite thus; else, if the teacher is not properly blazing, first —
By expiations, gifts, breath-controls, having purified, perform this rite and initiation without doubt.
The tattva-knower frees beasts by will in every case; Śiva directly — so worship him always.
No deceit here; doing so sends the disciple downward. Never proclaim his sin; the proclaimer falls.
Avoid hell — thus the Dīkṣottara rite. This absent-initiation is twofold: for the living and the other.

rasa.dominant: karuṇa (compassion) with śānta weight (redemption of the absent and the dead; rest in the installed form)
rasa.sthayibhava: karuṇa (compassion) in the guru's act of uplifting
rasa.justification: The ahnika redeems the absent and the dead through the guru's compassion; the installed form rests, and wonder at the net-practice crowns the rite.

sections.SUMMARY: Now the initiation-rite of the one situated in absence is described. For accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation one is led to the true guru: in this Mālinī sentence 'prati' is expressive of facing-towards. Facing-towards of the disciple consists in becoming the seat of his grace; the saying 'worshipping him' is an indicator of the cause of grace. From that connection then someone is liberated instantly: thus is also the meaning of this jewel of the Mālinī sentence. 'In that instant' means there is no further moment of desire to approach; but exactly thus the guru, struck by compassion, should uplift him. Of one who, body wasted by guru-service, died without obtaining initiation — or whose desire arose at the moment of death. Or of one who shared the initiation-rites of lower tantras etc., having obtained samaya-status, (but) not having obtained the supreme initiation. Of one struck by a ḍimba, or devoured by a yogeśī through sorcery, or slain by yantra-tantra etc. by the guru — the dead. Of one who, having obtained initiation, violated his samaya — even so, through the vehement entreaty of relatives, wife, friends, sons. Or by itself, by the force of compassion arisen towards that person even, (of one) who is the bearer of a portion of śaktipāta come towards him known. The guru should perform the initiation redeeming the dead, bestowing Śiva; that is said by the Supreme Lord in Śrī-Mṛtyuñjaya-Siddha and the rest. For the uninitiated, king and the rest, the lazy, the fallen, the dead, child, sick, woman, old — and one should arrange the redemption of the dead. The rite all previously told: that is desired to be concise, devoid of guru-and-other worship, in the external for enjoyment, because it. Preliminary consecration, caru, field, bed, maṇḍala-preparation are not useful here; (they are) for the disciple's purification and dream-seeing. But the maṇḍala is for making mantras present and satisfied; and on the following day the worship of gods is not directly helpful for this. Through rite, instrument, place, maṇḍala, form, mantra; through meditation, union, sole devotion, knowledge, identification — (these are the causes of presence). Of one who entered into that, of disciples and of the guru also: these eleven are told as causes for presence. Higher and higher superior, also from freedom from mixture: the rite abundantly, flowers and the rest, superior, endowed with marks. Single liṅga and the rest as place, where the self is pleased; the maṇḍala three-trident-lotus-wheel, which in mantra-maṇḍala. Even when not invoked, seen — the accomplishment of samaya-status of the good; that is said in the Mālinī-tantra: accomplished samaya-maṇḍala. By which, as soon as seen — thus, from the two words 'siddha' and 'mātra': the form radiant in form, which, mantra like it very radiant. The rest is clearly therefore not told here in detail again; having made the maṇḍala, having worshipped the god there with kuśa grass — and. With cow-dung he should make the form, disciple-like, should place; then in it one path to be purified, from the contemplation of pervasion. Having deposited up to prakṛti, again he should perform the rite by the great-net-practice, from the middle of all the paths. Having drawn the mind situated there — should do: that rite is said. Having risen from the mūlādhāra, the rod of the path of the vast spread endless nāḍī, having occupied by vigor, reached the nose-sky, throwing, desires to pervade up to the wheel of the path with a net of smoke-beautiful dense tips, covering — bringing the desired life — thus: the practice called the great net. By this to-be-covered goes dependence on another; facing-towards-ness at first; is led to five, if all — then from the middle of the path as desired, in drawing and extracting, or in the matter of the dead person to be drawn — then in the living, yoga called the net, taught in the Śrī-Śaṃbhunātha-āgama, spoken by me. When long broken apart, as two armies joined: again horse, elephant, man run towards their own caste by taste; by the nāḍī-wheels with the instrument-winds just so, joined, each with its own taste unified, by their own net subjugated. Drawn by the great net, the living soul, by the knowing one, releases heaven, ghost, animal, hell — then at that time this one. Obtained by that knowledge-mantra-yoga, this person also, artificial, like a yogī, then from the heart of the sādhya abandons identification. The states from immobile etc., wondrous, nearness to that world — should abandon, thus: not wonder; he thus who, by action even, or. From being in an eligible body, in humanity — but bodied, not then liberated; from body, at end of body, but should go to Śiva. In that body but some of his arises: supreme Śāṅkara grace, from root and from knowledge or from served teacher. Situated in that body, even this living soul, by net-force etc. this, pervades the body of darbha and the rest, by own abiding even unconscious. By the force of abundant yoga-mantra-rite-knowledge again, even the human body this one then immediately releases. Even sleeping-like, even bodiless, who is living soul: he even, drawn from the net, comes to the darbha body, of fruit, and or. Jasmine fruit and the rest, whatever by that, or body-fashioning: by suitability both inside and outside, that here superior is said. Then the living soul brought by the net method stands as if asleep, from absence of obtaining apparatus of mind-endowed body and the rest. It neither vibrates nor knows nor speaks nor certainly desires; for such a one indeed, all purificatory rites as before should prepare. By seedless initiation yoga, all having done the previously-told rite producing union, with full oblation together, should throw and him. In the body of darbha and the rest, offered into the fire of mantra together with full, freed from bonds goes to Śiva, free from return again. Furnished with proof but this, where the darbha-born body vibrates: there, by the yoga of offering prāṇa, mind, mantra, so may happen. Of the one with practice that also is said (breathing force); not for that, by the same means as redemption of the dead, as possible, by means. Initiation of living absent also to be performed, seedless but it: in it, in fashioning form resembling darbha, from net-yoga. Drawing by imagination alone of the living soul, from fear of death: the rest as before, without burning kuśa and the rest form. From limitedness and non-lordship in the sādhya, from niyati-constraint, net-drawing without practice, from attachment and aversion not, arises. Absent: indeed by unequal initiations if initiated, there superior may be mighty; for purification but the inferior. In the union for enjoyment but, by many gurus so, when performed, variety of enjoyment from variety of causes. In initiation of absent, beyond māyā, for enjoyment should join; desire for enjoyment rare indeed being, or for cessation of enjoyment. Said indeed: of own and other consciousness, own consciousness more powerful in overriding; that which overrides, of equality and indifference so. Venerable Dharmaśiva said: in absence, in the karma procedure, in initiation of absent, properly, in the full oblation rite, if. Fire emits ciṭi-ciṭā sound with smoke, bears blue-cloud-color, repeatedly blazes, subsides. Detail, terrible form and, runs on earth and downwards; or crow-etc unheard sound: then him the guru should mark. By brahmin-killing and the rest, by sins and by association with them minor sins: then of him not to be done, initiation in this unperformed rite. Nine-souled, standing inside the phaṭ cavity, again endowed with five phaṭs: of so-and-so thus, sins, I burn according to eight phaṭs. Thus thousand-fold fire-offering to be done with sesame and rice; at the end full and to be given; then to him by initiation the guru. Up to the supreme goal should do purification of principles; even in direct presence of the paśu situated, of the sinner, Bhagavan-filled. Power of the one who obtained: the eldest, exactly thus rite should perform; if or the teacher properly not blazing of him before that. By expiations so, by gifts, by breath-controls and, purification having done, this rite and also initiation should perform without doubt. In every way being even, the tattva-knower liberates beasts by will alone; Śiva directly — therefore him should worship always. Deceit there not to be done; and having done that downwards should go the disciple. Not again should proclaim of him sin; the proclaimer should go. Hell should avoid — therefore thus in Dīkṣottara rite. This initiation of absent twofold told, by division of living and other.
sections.FUNCTION: Establishes parokṣa-dīkṣā: initiation of the absent and the dead — the guru draws the soul through the net (mahājāla) into a darbha-form, performs seedless initiation, and liberates; the living absent is initiated by imagination alone; compassion (karuṇā) is the engine.
sections.KEY TERMS: parokṣa-dīkṣā (initiation of the absent), mṛtoddhāra (redemption of the dead), mahājāla (great net), darbha-form, śaktipāta (descent of grace), samaya (vow), nirbīja (seedless), pūrṇāhuti (full oblation), parokṣa (absent), jīvat-parokṣa (living absent), pratyaya (proof/vibration), jāla (net), karuṇā (compassion), māyā (māyā), bhoga (enjoyment), mokṣa (liberation)
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Ahnika 21 is the Tantraloka parokṣa-dīkṣā chapter (initiation of the absent/dead): 61 units, 460 tokens.
